scheme: Version 1.<improvements>.<fixes>: the minor number counts the improvements and the patch number counts the fixes since the first release (1.0.0). Add an entry for every improvement or fix; the version is calculated from this list.

changes.title: Fabric MCP Studio: build Fabric data foundations by chatting with your own Copilot
Fixes from live testing: ontology names, tenant checks, only report changes that were saved, layout
Ontology questions turned off until Fabric answers them reliably; numbers come from the semantic model
AdventureWorksDW2022 sample created as a Fabric SQL database
Desktop shortcut and single-instance launch
Tidy job cards; jobs cut off by a restart are reported as interrupted
Copilot embedded in every step; silent launcher
Data tab shows the connected source in full
Apply Copilot's semantic model suggestions in one click
Reports & apps: professional Power BI reports from templates and themes
Report recommendations and one-click Apply for Copilot's report suggestions
Business rules (ontology) dashboard
Org app that bundles the reports for the organization
Built reports and the app shown at the top of Reports & apps
Copilot sign-in works when a GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable is set
Real-time: live events, Eventhouse and Real-Time Dashboard
Live ontology and Activator alerts on rule breaks
Planning: budgets and forecasts with Fabric planning
Up-front checks: capacity, role and tenant settings per tab
Clean up asks for a typed confirmation and refreshes every tab
Solution map: lineage of everything the studio builds
Real-time setup waits until there is data to shape the events
Medallion architecture (Bronze, Silver, Gold) for the live events, shown as a Fabric task flow
Data prep notebook (Python) for any lakehouse: names, fixes, relationships, measures and charts
Saving the project retries when Windows briefly locks the file
Suggested questions built from your model, reports, rules, plan and live data
Fabric plan no longer bound to a connection that can't open the model; plans on a recreated model are fixed
Fabric data agent created and published by the studio, with Apply suggestions
Disclaimer for internal and external users, shown once and in the footer; What's new
Version number calculated from the improvements and fixes
Clean up empties the project: the map shows Choose a workspace instead of the old workspace
Naming standard [Domain]_[Object]_[Purpose]_[Environment] for every item, from what the environment is for
An Apply button under every Copilot recommendation that waits for your go-ahead, not only models, reports and data agents
Solution map labels no longer touch the parts: they wrap or step aside when the columns are narrow
Planning says in plain words why a data source can't hold the plan and how to fix it; default dimensions skip ones too detailed to plan
Planning on lakehouses: plan values in a planning warehouse, read by the lakehouse through a OneLake shortcut
Medallion task flow (Bronze, Silver, Gold) for the existing items, from Fabric's predesigned template
GitHub Copilot only in developer mode; Azure AI Foundry / Azure OpenAI is the default AI provider
Fabric plan: Who can plan shows the workspace roles and gives Contributor access; the plan card says which account a plan reads the model as and how to fix it
Plan help: the connection sign-in window may pick your Windows account on its own – choose Use another account
Who can plan gives Member access to the account saved in a shared connection (Fabric: DMTS Connection Owner Missing)
Fabric plans connect to the model with the planner's own sign-in (Data › Add › Connect); no deprecated shared connection, and Recreate without a connection for old plans
Remove buttons for every item, disabled while something uses it; Items in this project shows what uses what
Your own Power BI templates: upload .pbit, .pbix, zipped Power BI projects, report layouts and themes; reports are bound to your semantic model with fields matched by name
Items in this project fits its column: long names wrap, no horizontal scrollbar
Items in this project no longer touches the Activity button

Task flows: use the task flow already in your workspace or one of Fabric's predesigned flows (Medallion, Basic data analytics, Event analytics, Event medallion, Lambda, Basic machine learning models); every item goes to its box, you can move items, and the flow stays up to date
Several semantic models per project: design new ones or add existing models from any workspace, switch the active model, and reports, data agent, org app and answers follow it
Semantic models pop-up: double-click Semantic model on the map to switch the active model, add an existing model or start a new one

Each data source keeps its own items: choosing another source shows its own items on the map (or greys them out), the previous one keeps everything and you can switch back; another workspace starts everything over
Double-click works on the map: Data source lists the data in the workspace and the project's sources; the workspace name lists the workspaces on the capacity
Check and fix a semantic model's data: finds keys that repeat on the one side of a relationship and removes exact copies in a warehouse (with a backup), then reloads the model

After an update the studio says a newer version is installed and restarts itself with Restart now, instead of failing with "Not found" (for example the data source list); Fabric system databases are no longer listed as data sources

An existing semantic model brings what is built on it to the map: its Power BI reports, the data agents that answer from it and the lakehouse or warehouse it reads (in place when the project has no data). They are shown as existing items and never changed

After duplicates are removed, the model reloads until it holds the fixed data (it could keep the old rows and keep failing); the check compares the model with its data and offers Reload the model, and no longer shows "null"
Reports use the real year column: a hidden year (such as CalendarYear) instead of Week Number Of Year, so trends and "full years" are right

Maps in reports: when the model has countries, states, cities, postal codes or latitude/longitude, the studio adds a Map page (Azure Maps bubbles sized by the main measure, drill down country › state › city) to the Executive report and recommends a Regional report
No more command windows flashing on every click after Restart now: sign-in calls to the Azure CLI always run hidden, and the studio restarts in a hidden console like the desktop icon

User Guide (PDF) for people without a technical background: installing, starting, every step of the app with screenshots, troubleshooting and a quick reference card (docs/Fabric-MCP-Studio-User-Guide.pdf)
No stray "null" text on the Data, Real-time and Semantic model pages and in Copilot's Apply cards

Live events bind to the ontology again: the live tables hold only the key, the event time and the live values, so Fabric no longer rejects them (BackingColumnOrphanedByNameCollision for Segment, Region, Category…); the medallion layers re-point them the same way

With several semantic models, Plan vs actual is offered and built only on the model the plan is on, and the ontology's business rules and the sample's questions only on models built on that data; rules are counted once
The Real-time cards query the Eventhouse only while the Real-time page is open and live data exists, slow down after errors, and stop after clean up
A report is never overwritten from another data source: report names used by every data source of the workspace, and existing reports found on their models, are kept free
Restart now works in folders with accented names, and the running studio stops only once the new copy has started – otherwise it keeps running and says why
Security: the studio answers only when it is opened as 127.0.0.1 or localhost, and accepts changes only from its own pages (protects the session token against DNS rebinding)
Items built without a data source stay reachable when such a set is already kept (their own entry in Data sources)
After a data fix, a second model table on the same warehouse table (a role-playing dimension) no longer keeps the reload waiting for minutes

Solution map: the reports node counts the active model's reports (and says how many are on other models), a configured part whose last change failed is marked with what went wrong, and the org app says which reports aren't in it yet
Item names in the Data sources pop-up wrap after underscores instead of in the middle of a word; the planning log counts the members the plan has (no blank member)

Clearer messages: unknown report pages are named with the valid ones, Fabric validation errors are one plain sentence per issue (Fabric's raw answer is folded under Details), and a task flow that is gone says Medallion is shown instead
Reports & apps shows the reports that aren't in the org app yet, with Update the app

Restart now works when the studio was started from the desktop icon: the new copy writes to the log file that is free (studio.log or studio.restart.log) – before, it couldn't open the log the running copy held, never started, and the studio stopped

Installer you can share as a zip: checks the prerequisites (installed, missing or too old), installs the missing ones (Git, Node.js LTS; optionally Azure CLI and GitHub CLI) with winget or from the vendor, downloads the app from the repository (GitHub sign-in for a private one; a zip without Git), installs its packages and the desktop shortcut; running it again updates and keeps your data;     check-only and uninstall included (installer/build-installer.ps1)

OpenRouter as an AI provider in developer mode: one API key for hundreds of models, a searchable list of the models that can call tools with their prices and context, OpenRouter's Auto Router as the default, and the model picker in the Copilot header

A paused capacity is checked every minute (a running one every five minutes while a page is open): once it is resumed the map, the badges and every page light up again by themselves, with a toast – no reload or Check again

A semantic model on the data prep notebook's curated lakehouse uses what the notebook found: keys, roles, every relationship (dates included, so the date table is marked) and its KPIs as measures; the notebook's KPIs and DataQuality tables stay out
Readable primary buttons and selected toggles in the dark themes (dark text on the light accent colors)
Removing the data prep notebook or a data source no longer deletes a curated lakehouse that another data source of the workspace uses: it stays and Remove says who uses it
Recommended report names on a second model all start with the model's name when a plain name is taken, and reports found in Fabric on the model count as taken
Page errors are in plain words too: a model whose data is gone says so instead of showing the request and Fabric's raw JSON
Data sources pop-up: a source whose item is no longer in Fabric says so instead of “in another workspace”
Pop-ups close with the Esc key (approvals still need an answer)
Turning developer mode off while the studio runs switches GitHub Copilot or OpenRouter to Azure AI Foundry right away, open chats included; turning it on again brings the saved choice back
Installer: uninstall with -KeepData keeps the data when the folder is given with a trailing backslash (it was moved inside the folder and deleted with it)
Settings: saving GitHub Copilot after looking at OpenRouter no longer saves OpenRouter's model or key for GitHub
OpenRouter: the prompt and the answer always fit the model's context (the answer gets at most a quarter), and a conversation that is too long says so in plain words
Restart now: two restarts in a row can't leave two studios on the same data folder (each restart has its own handshake, and a late copy stops instead of taking another port)
Installer: a copy installed from the zip is updated once Git is there (it switches to Git updates, keeping studio\data), and a studio closed for an update is started again when the update fails

Reports the studio built on an existing model (by another copy of the studio, or before the project was started over) are recognised by their description in Fabric: they are the project's again – with their theme and pages – instead of “Existing report”, so they can be rebuilt and go in the org app
The org app is easy to find: Your reports has an Org app row with Create app (or what it needs first), and the Org app part of the map opens Reports & apps at it instead of the top of the page

Org apps show their reports: the studio gives the app an audience with the overview and every report (without one Fabric shows “No items to show”, even to its owner); Update app adds it to apps made before

Create app asks which reports go in the org app – the studio's reports on the model are ticked, and reports already on the model in the workspace can be added (the app only links to them); Choose reports changes them later, and Copilot asks first too
Delete app on Reports & apps deletes the org app and its audience (the reports stay)

The Data sources pop-up opens on the project workspace and has a workspace list: pick any workspace to see its lakehouses, warehouses and databases and use one in place; a line says where the active data source (and the others) read their data, with Show

A dropped network connection no longer looks like a permission problem: calls to Fabric and Power BI that only read (and reading a model's definition or querying it) are tried again when the connection drops, changes only when they never left the computer; when the network stays down the message says so instead of "fetch failed – you need Contributor"
Uninstalling a copy of the studio removes only the shortcuts that open that copy: a desktop or Start menu shortcut with the same name to another copy (installed in another folder) is kept
Copilot can render inline charts in the chat window with a studio-chart block, so a request for a chart or graph no longer has to create a Power BI report unless the user asks for one

Inline chat visuals support many chart types and dashboards: bar, horizontal/stacked bar, line, area, pie/donut, scatter/bubble, heatmap, treemap, waterfall, KPI cards, tables and multi-visual dashboard grids

New Costs tab: a friendly capacity utilization and cost dashboard over the Microsoft Fabric Capacity Metrics app, with heavy hitters, workspace/user/background usage, smoothing/overage guidance, recommendations, and pay-as-you-go vs reservation estimates
Costs page is easier to read: compact KPI cards, readable ranked bars for heavy hitters, and clear empty-state cards instead of tiny zero-value chart axes
Costs cards no longer show fake 0% values when the Capacity Metrics app has no timepoint rows: they show Not available and use item-history CU-hours/top-item data instead
When Microsoft Fabric Capacity Metrics is missing, the Costs tab opens the supported Microsoft AppSource install flow and explains that a capacity admin must finish Install and Connect in Fabric

Costs page balances visuals and readability: visual summary cards are back, ranked lists are spaced out, cards use useful data instead of fake zeros, and recommendations name the top artifact, workspace, operation and tuning actions
Costs operation details now show where each high-cost operation comes from: top artifact, workspace, item type and explicit tuning actions in both the visual evidence list and operation table
Costs recommendations are easier to scan: the long numbered list is now compact action cards with labels, priority numbers and a small utilization checklist
The header subtitle now shows only the signed-in account, not the tenant name repeated next to it
The header context is cleaner: account, AI provider, workspace and model are shown as labeled chips that wrap instead of one long line

Clean up resources no longer fails at the end after deleting items; the workspace name is kept for the final message, deleted task flows are handled cleanly, and malformed task-flow metadata is ignored

GitHub Copilot sign-in no longer starts a new device-login prompt when GitHub CLI is already signed in; it checks the existing gh session first and gives a useful error when Copilot access is still not accepted
Reports profile now returns the expected user-facing Create the semantic model first state instead of a server error when no semantic model exists
Settings has a Diagnostics card that downloads a redacted troubleshooting bundle with version, project summary, readiness, jobs, activity and recent logs
Safe demo mode (STUDIO_DEMO=1) uses mock Fabric data and blocks writes for training/screenshots, and npm run smoke starts that mode to regression-check key endpoints without touching Fabric
Audit log is now a smaller fixed-height card with its own scrollbar and sticky filter header, so the Activity page is easier to scan
